name: Sports interview (press-conference answer)
what: A single seated person at a branded press-conference table answering questions from off-camera reporters, filmed from the press seats — one unbroken set-up, the whole read carried by the words and the subject's face.

specialised.what: ONE set-up, one room, two framings only — a wide walk-in with reporters' heads in the foreground and a static medium on the subject held for the rest of the piece
specialised.why: the frame map reads 90.007 s with 0 cuts and a single shot K01 (eye level, medium, set down still, no move); the shot table changes framing once, at 0:04.2, and never again. Every clip comes off one or two pictures of the same table

specialised.what: only the subject is ever generated — three of the five cast members are voices with no face
specialised.why: the cast sheet marks Moderator, the two reporters 'Not seen' on face, hair, body, wardrobe; the Staff Member appears as a torso and arms for one second (0:10–0:11). No person pictures are owed for them, which is the cheapest cast list of any family we have

specialised.what: the off-camera questions and announcements are voice-only tracks over the subject's listening clip — no reverse shots, no reporter pictures
specialised.why: the shot table never cuts to a questioner: 0:20.9–0:46.7 is 25.8 s of a reporter talking over a static medium of the subject listening. Phase 2's own note is 'a long, unbroken 25-second hold'

specialised.what: listening is a scene, not dead air — the longest single stretch (25.8 s) is the subject reacting while someone else speaks
specialised.why: `B-vo` carries 46.9 s of 90 against `A`'s 42.1 s. More than half the runtime is the subject silent on camera, so the clip plan has to hold identity and micro-expression with the mouth closed

specialised.what: nothing to camera — the subject looks at whoever asked, then scans the room; never into the lens
specialised.why: signature address is to-each-other, and the cast note reads 'Maintains steady eye contact with the person asking the question, then scans the room while answering'. A to-lens look reads as an ad and kills the broadcast premise

specialised.what: no product anywhere in the piece — product_role is none; the offer lands in the caption, the comments or the endcard the lane adds, never in the room
specialised.why: props are a microphone, a water bottle and a name card; nothing in the teardown touches a product. This is the first family where the picture prompts owe no product-scale or product-colour rule at all

specialised.what: the branded backdrop and table skirt are the whole production value — an original institutional backdrop (repeating logo pattern, matching table cloth, bright flat front light, no shadow on the wall), built once as a set element and reused for every piece in this family
specialised.why: the places read says the backdrop and skirt 'provide immediate institutional authority… forcing the viewer to accept the premise as reality'. The swipe's real team and sponsor marks are the swipe's, not ours (holds follow the swipe — flaggable things become original stand-ins), so one banked original backdrop replaces them and amortises across every press-conference ad

specialised.what: broadcast capture look is explicit in every picture prompt: tripod eye level from the press seats, reporters' heads soft in the foreground of the wide, hard even frontal studio light, no grade, no bokeh, no phone-grade realism
specialised.why: capture is 'broadcast', not 'studio' or 'phone'. The aesthetic archetype is 'authentic sports journalism… harsh lighting, step-and-repeat banners'. The nearest playbook's phone-grade style lock would read as the wrong genre here

specialised.what: room sound is the signature: continuous camera shutters under the whole piece, with faint shuffle and a laugh beat where the room reacts
specialised.why: every row of the shot table carries 'room: heavy camera shutters', and 0:15.4–0:20.9 adds 'faint laughter from reporters'. Nine added effects were measured. Shutters are the cheapest and strongest realism cue in this format and are a bed, not a cue

specialised.what: music is a low ambient drone under the voices for the full runtime, not the nearest playbook's ducked bed — measured 92.3 bpm, F minor, textural rather than beat-driven, one subtle build around 22 s, ending quietly
specialised.why: the music read: 'dark, atmospheric ambient drone… low, ominous synthesizer pads and sub-bass rumbles… the rhythm is very loose and textural rather than beat-driven'. A rhythmic bed would fight the press-room realism and expose the piece as an ad

specialised.what: lower thirds are the only on-screen text, white, on the cut at 0:04.2 for about four seconds — place card, then name and role; no captions at all
specialised.why: the layer sheet lists exactly two lower thirds and 'Hook text: none / Captions: none'. Captions on a press conference look like a repost, not a broadcast, so the ig-fb-native caption look is off for this family

specialised.what: the hook is the premise, not a line — the opener is the wide walk-in and the impossible pairing of person and uniform; alternate openings swap the premise (who, in what, where) rather than rewriting the first spoken line
specialised.why: psychological play 1 is 'The Pattern Interrupt (Visual)'. Phase 1's purpose is to 'arrest attention through a highly unexpected visual'. The nearest playbook's hook alternates swap a scene or a line; here the swappable unit is the premise itself

specialised.what: the subject's spoken delivery keeps the hesitation — 'um', 'uh', 'you know', a thought narrated while it forms, softeners before absolutes — and the voice is cast for a mid-low, calm, resonant, measured read
specialised.why: the voice fingerprint: 'Frequent use of "Um", "Uh", and "you know" as connective tissue'; 'Narrates the way in, buying time to formulate the answer'. A clean, fluent read is the single fastest way this family reads as AI

specialised.what: clips at 1080p for the subject, but clip length pushed to the 10 s ceiling and several clips off ONE picture — the static medium is the same picture all the way through, restarted with a small punch-in at each join
specialised.why: zero cuts across 90 s means every join is ours, not the swipe's. One approved medium picture can carry 6–8 clips at 1–2 clips per picture elsewhere; this family supports 4+ off a single frame, which is where its cost advantage comes from

specialised.what: two pictures total as the floor: the wide walk-in and the static medium. No per-scene pictures
specialised.why: one setting, one shot, one subject. The nearest playbook budgets 108+39 picture calls on a multi-room family; the shot table here supports two framings and nothing else

specialised.what: a hands-and-props pass on the medium picture — gooseneck mic, water bottle, folded tent name card — because the subject's business in the scene is handling them
specialised.why: the props list times each one (water handed in at 0:10, the card picked up at 0:15.4 and set down at 0:19.0) and the manner note is 'adjusts his seating and microphone with familiarity'. These small handled objects are where extra fingers and warped text show up

specialised.what: the name card, the backdrop logos and any sponsor patch are the only readable text in frame and must be our own words, spelled right, checked at full resolution before any clip
specialised.why: the clip gate already refuses a misspelt name or big text that is not words. Here legible text is in three places at once (card, backdrop pattern, jersey patch) and it is the first thing a viewer reads

specialised.what: a real-person likeness gate before anything spends: the subject is a banked original character, never a recognisable public figure in a situation they were not in
specialised.why: the triage read on this swipe is 'Impossible scenario… indicates a deepfake… LIKELY AI'. The structure — press conference, unexpected announcement, slow reveal — is what carries over; the swipe's actual person does not

stage_order: writing (the premise is the hook; the answer carries the message)
elements (one subject, one backdrop set, three props — three voices with no face)
voices (every speaker, including the three never seen)
clips (Omni 1080p, many off one picture, on-camera lines in the clip)
edit (shutter bed, drone under, lower thirds, cover before remake)

audio.on_camera: said inside the clip, then speech-to-speech into the subject's cloned voice + crisp finish
audio.off_camera: the moderator's and each reporter's cloned voice on its own track — no picture is ever owed for them
audio.turns: strict turn-taking with a beat of room tone between — a reporter finishes completely before the answer starts (the swipe withholds the answer until the question ends)
audio.delivery: keep the fillers and the self-interruptions; mid-low, calm, measured, resonant for the subject; mid-pitch professional for the moderator and reporters
audio.room_tone: continuous camera shutters under the entire piece, laid as a bed before the music

framings: wide walk-in: subject entering from frame left, reporters' heads and shoulders soft in the foreground, backdrop visible behind
static medium: subject seated centre, mic in front, backdrop filling the frame behind
pictures.subject_zone: 15–85% of the height, said in the first prompt
pictures.style_lock: broadcast press capture — tripod eye level from the press seats, hard even frontal studio light, no shadow on the backdrop, no grade, no shallow depth, no phone-grade look
pictures.set_reuse: one banked original backdrop + table skirt element, reused across every piece in this family
pictures.only_these_things: list every prop — gooseneck mic on a desktop stand, water bottle, folded tent name card, table cloth; nothing from the swipe's own marks, team or sponsor leaks in
pictures.text_in_frame: only our own words on the name card and backdrop pattern — spelled, checked at full resolution
pictures.product: none — this format has no product in the room

clips.cut_at: line or sentence boundaries, never padded
clips.person_from: the approved medium picture for every seated beat; the approved wide for the walk-in only
clips.restart_on_same_picture: 7% punch-in so the join reads as a jump cut — the swipe has zero cuts, so every join is ours to hide
clips.listening_clips: the longest clips in the piece carry no speech — the subject listens, chin on hand, eyes on the questioner; no mouth movement at all
clips.camera: static in every clip, one continuous take, no reframe inside a call

cast.reuse: banked cast first — one subject carries every piece in this family; the moderator and the reporters are banked VOICES only, no faces owed
cast.likeness: banked original character — never a recognisable public figure placed in a situation they were not in
cast.product: when our version hands the subject the product: real size from the turntable, pasted from real photos

hooks.shape: the premise IS the hook — alternates swap who walks in, what they are wearing and whose backdrop it is, not the first line
hooks.generated: only the wide walk-in picture and its clip

captions.look: none — a press conference with burned-in captions reads as a repost, not a broadcast
captions.lower_thirds: two, white, in on the cut at ~4 s for ~4 s: place line top left, name and role bottom left

apply: line parity on every talking clip
mouths reviewed — the subject's lips must be still through every listening clip
picture QC with a working reviewer
readable-text check on the name card, backdrop and any patch at full resolution
likeness check — no recognisable public figure
skip: product-scale and product-colour checks (no product in frame)

edit.method: video-edit machine cut on the voice track
edit.broll: real footage only, ~2.5 s each — customer before/afters and the product in use; no AI clips, no burned-in text (the owner 2026-10-09)
edit.lip_offset: measure in each clip's own frames; one global picture offset when the whole cut is a frame off
edit.music: low ambient drone under the whole piece, F-minor-dark and textural, one subtle build around 22 s, ending quietly — about -22 dB under voice, quieter than a rhythmic bed
edit.room_bed: camera shutters continuous under everything; a faint laugh beat where the room reacts
edit.joins: every join is ours (the swipe has zero cuts) — 7% punch-in at each restart so it reads as a broadcast cut, never a glitch
edit.end_card: none (the owner 2026-10-09: "forget the end card, it's weird")

failures.failure: the picture door refused a public figure's likeness
failures.fix: re-sent once with the swipe frame's faces covered; the subject is an original banked character

failures.failure: Omni refused the same 3 clips on every try
failures.fix: those clips went to the alternate door (Seedance) with the subject's real cloned voice

failures.failure: an invented name card in a picture
failures.fix: fixed at the picture — name card text is ours, checked at full resolution

failures.failure: the frame map found only 12 moments with 40 s gaps on the single-camera swipe; production improvised
failures.fix: frame map in 8-second windows on a single locked shot (67 moments)

failures.failure: the cut went away to the press pack
failures.fix: one fixed wide camera, one take — no cutaways; chained start and end frames

failures.failure: overlapping 'uh/um' murmurs cut off a name
failures.fix: no overlap — each speaker waits their turn

failures.failure: a false 2-frame lip slip — the checker counted 30 fps on 24 fps clips
failures.fix: lip offset measured in each clip's own frames

watch_for: the subject's lips moving through a 20-second listening clip — the longest clips in this format have no speech at all
the clip model drifting the face or beard across a long static hold, so the person at 1:20 is not the person at 0:20
the backdrop logo pattern rendering as garbled near-letters, which is unreadable at full size and obvious at the top of the feed
the name card's text misspelt or warped — it is held up to the lens on purpose, so it is read
the clip model adding a camera move or a reframe inside a call, when the whole format is one locked-off tripod
a third hand or a warped hand on the mic, the water bottle or the name card — the subject handles all three
the mouth tracker locking onto a foreground reporter's head instead of the seated subject
a to-lens look creeping in, which turns a press conference into an ad read
the fillers scrubbed out of the voice, leaving a fluent delivery that reads as synthetic
the backdrop, light or table dressing changing between the wide and the medium, so it stops being one room
the shutter bed dropping out at a join, which is the loudest possible tell that the cut is assembled
the music becoming beat-driven and turning the room into an ad bed
the room laugh landing where nothing funny happened, or missing where the line earns it
a reporter or the moderator appearing on screen — they are voices only, and a face owes a whole cast entry
the premise swapping in a real identifiable person, which is the likeness wall, not a creative choice

cost.why: one room, one subject, two pictures and no product — the whole piece runs off 4–8 clips per picture on a locked-off static frame, with three of five speakers costing voice only and the backdrop banked once and reused
cost.measured: r1 $__, r2 $__, r3 ~$__ (Omni 1080p + pictures, ledger.json each)

quality_bar: one room all the way through — same backdrop pattern, same light, same table dressing, same wardrobe
the camera never moves and never reframes inside a shot; only two framings exist in the finished ad
the subject's lips are completely still whenever someone else is speaking
every word is heard, none cut off, and the hesitations are still there
the subject sounds like their face — mid-low, calm, measured, in their own cloned voice
the moderator and the reporters are never seen, only heard
the name card, the backdrop text and any patch are our own words, spelled right and readable at full size
the subject looks at whoever asked, then scans the room — never into the lens
no third hand, nothing warped on the mic, the bottle or the card
camera shutters run unbroken under the entire piece, including across every join
the music is a low drone under the voices and never turns into a beat
the lower thirds appear once, on the early cut, and never return
no product is visible in the room at any point
the person in the last clip is the same person as in the first
